findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

During the inspection a food handler was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC. They are instructed to pass on needed food safety education to those in the facility that need it. Ensure that hand washing takes place correctly at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

A can of mushrooms was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler opened and with a moldy layer observed on the top of the foods. The PIC was shown and threw away the foods to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored in such a way so as to protect them from contamination. They should also be used prior to the point that pathogenic organisms begin to grow in the containers.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw beef and raw chicken were observed over raw shrimp in the standing cooler between the mop sink and hallway. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the shrimp moved to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored according to their cooking temperatures in the facility so as to ensure that the safety of the customers is maintained.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani bucket would not register the CL sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. When asked the PIC indicated that the sanitizer was made in the morning. The inspector stated that the chemical breaks down even if no use is taking place and quicker with use. The bucket needs to be remade regularly throughout the day so as to remain at effective concentration to reduce biological contamination concerns on the surfaces. The bucket was remade to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

1) A can of pineapples was observed opened and with rust having formed on the inside of the can. The PIC was shown and discarded the container (and foods) to correct. 2) A can of sliced olives was observed opened and with approximately 1/3 left in the can. The can does not appear to be degrading at the time of the inspection. The PIC was shown and allowed to move the olives into another container and place a lid on it to correct. Both items were observed in the bottom section of the prep cooler. Ensure that all foods are stored in containers that have lids/seals that protect them from miscellaneous sources of contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Grease was observed with numerous dead flies stuck in it on the wall between the hand sink and vent above. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that the facility is maintained clean at all times.

findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC was notified and supplied paper towels to the sink to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the bathroom was without readily accessible soap. The PIC was notified and placed a new supply by the sink to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks in the facility are properly supplied at all times int he facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw eggs were observed over raw vegetables in the display cooler across from the cashier counter. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The cooler was re-arranged during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored according to their safe cooking temperatures at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several knives and pans stored as clean and ready for use were observed with food debris remaining or with sticky/oily residues remaining. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct the immediate violation. They should review dish washing procedures with employees and ensure that all food contact surfaces are being completely cleaned each time that they are washed.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

Containers of bleach and cleaning agents are observed on shelves above drinks intended for consumers. The PIC was shown and the location discussed. The shelves were re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Ensure safe storage locations in the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A container of rice in the standing cooler in the hallway is observed with an internal temperature of 50F. Per the PIC the container is from the day before. After discussion the container was discarded to correct the current issue. A follow up is already scheduled to manage the cooler not functioning correctly.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

One of the containers (re-used from previous sauces) of house made sauce is observed with mold colonies inside of the container. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all foods are stored in clean containers and that they are protected from pathogenic growth at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several knives and pans in storage as clean and ready for use are observed with food debris remaining. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct the immediate violation. They should review dish washing procedures with employees and ensure that all food contact surfaces are being completely cleaned each time that they are washed.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A)TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

On arrival, several TCS items in the standing cooler in the bathroom hallway are observed with internal temperatures between 56F and 61F. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they stated that employees were probably in an out regularly, increasing the temperature. The inspector stated that, while that would increase the ambient air temperature of the cooler, the foods should not be out of temperature long enough for the internal temperatures to rise to these levels. The TCS foods in this cooler were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Foods discarded include cooked rice, cooked pork chop, sausage, sauces labeled “refrigerate after opening” and house made sauces including oil and garlic in their ingredients. A check of the cooler will take place to ensure the cooler is repaired/adjusted to function correctly (refer to line item #33).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The standing cooler in the bathroom hallway is observed to not be functioning correctly (refer to line item #22). The cooler needs maintenance/ adjustment to esnure safe food storage. Ensure that the cooler is functioning correctly prior to the follow-up in ten days.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: Ina a manner that is considered safe under the food code. Section (B) allows for TCS foods to be thawed completely submerged under running water.

On inspector arrival large blocks of frozen chicken are observed in standing water in the three part sink. Prior to discussion the primary manager arrived at the facility and corrected the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink in the kitchen is observed pulling away from the wall and exposing a large gap to the right of the sink. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair. Repair/seal the location to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface moving forward.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw chicken is observed over raw beef in the standing cooler to the right of the mop sink. Storage order for foods in a cooler was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure foods are stored in relation to their cooking temperatures so as to prevent possible cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket only registered at approximately 10 ppm on inspector test strips. The PIC stated that the bucket was made this morning. These chemicals will break down over time and require remaking throughout the day to maintain at effective concentration. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels throughout the day.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Cooked ground beef and gyro meat are observed in the bottom of the prep cooler without date marking. Per the PIC the items were prepared two days ago. Education was conducted and dates added to the containers to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) ready to eat (RTE) foods held at the facility longer than 24 hours are given date marks.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing during this inspection. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that food handlers wash hands at all times that hand washing is required.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw seafood and raw steak is observed over raw vegetables in the standing cooler in the hallway. The raw fish is also over RTE hot dogs in the same cooler. Education was conducted with the PIC and the items rearranged to comply with the code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label.

An employee was observed washing dishes without a sanitizing step included in the process. Knives specifically were observed to be scrubbed and rinsed then placed onto the magnetic rack for storage. Education was conducted with the PIC. Ensure that a sanitizing process is taking place after washing of each utensil and dish. This kills any remaining pathogens after the food contact surface is washed to remove the gross debris. The three part sink was reset and dishes re-washed with a sanitizing step involved to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

A partially used half gallon of milk in the standing cooler in the hallway is observed without a date marking. The item was opened two days ago. A date mark was added to correct the violation. Ensure that date marking is used for all RTE TCS foods in the facility.
